QC0 · HF4-B4 · SAVED SURFACES

From two horizons to a common horizon

55 common-horizon frames from 18.625M to 22M. Physical area was checked against diagnostics from the same run.

Yellow markers — approximately 5% of physical area with the largest deviation of the selected field from its weighted median. This describes QC0 fields; identity with the original HF1 structure has not been established.

Drag to rotate; use the wheel to zoom. “Orbit camera” changes the viewpoint at fixed time. The start and common-horizon buttons also select a suitable coordinate scale.

How to read this reconstruction

AH1/AH2 are individual apparent horizons. After common AH3 appears, they are shown only when enabled. Visible surfaces depend on the spatial slice: this is coordinate geometry, not an optical image or a reconstruction of the global event horizon.

τ is measured from the first saved AH3 at t=18.625M. No common horizon was found on the preceding saved slice, t=18.5625M. The exact time between these slices was not determined.

Fields are mapped only on the common horizon, with a fixed colour scale throughout the interval. Markers were calculated on the full 35×72 grid. Ψ₂ and σ components refer to the saved tetrad; null-direction normalisation affects σ.

For lightweight viewing, AH1/AH2 use a subset of nodes from the original six angular patches. Centre calculations use the full data. Two small grey caps close the AH3 display at the poles and are excluded from numerical analysis.

AH3 has no gaps over the available interval. AH1/AH2 are missing at t=0.375M, 16.8125M, 20.8125M and 21M. Earlier surfaces are not substituted. Playback stops at an empty pre-merger time; it can be passed manually.

Frame continuity and region overlap do not prove the motion of one material patch. A second numerical resolution and independence from arbitrary tetrad choices have not been tested here. QC0, SXS:BBH:0389 and SXS:BBH:0305 are different simulations.
